thread:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a p95 spike during the 02:30 canary that correlates with the new batching handoff change

maria: ugh, saw that too. this was the change that split prefill vs decode lanes, right?

tyler: yep. the split increases handshake churn when token budgets are short. i ran a quick profile with nvprof and the KV cache priming looked noisy

perf-bot: deploy 5623456001 succeeded to canary (eng-runtime). 12% p95 latency increase observed in canary region

alex: attaching the snippet i used to repro locally — small TTL on KV priming plus aggressive lane_count = 4 seems to trigger it:

```
# local batcher override
batching:
  lane_count: 4
  token_budget_per_lane: 32
  handshake_window_ms: 8
  kv_priming_ttl_ms: 100
```

maria: tyler, what did the kernel selection trace show? any unexpected kernel fallthroughs during the handoff?

tyler: yes — several gen-stage kernels falling back to slow_fused_attention under ~16 token sequences. That combined with frequent KV misses meant the runtime kept switching kernels mid-request which amplifies scheduling pressure

sam: can we try soft-fencing prefill lanes so they only steal microbatches when token_budget_per_lane >= 64? avoids tiny bursts

nina: i'd rather add a small hysteresis window on handshake_window_ms (like +5ms after a fallback) so we don't re-open the handshake too aggressively

alex: also noticed a regression in the token allocator: reclaimed slots had a 1.8x higher latency to reassign vs before. probably due to the new slot pool sharding. adding this to the perf regression ticket

maria: we should run a quick A/B in canary: A = revert lane_count to 2 + token_budget_per_lane 64; B = keep lane_count 4 but add handshake hysteresis + kv_priming backoff. measure p50/p95 and throughput per-GPU

tyler: i'll spin up both configs and instrument kernel-affinity traces + KV hit heatmap. goal: get p95 within 5% and preserve throughput within 3% of baseline

sam: FYI i pushed a tiny scheduler tweak that adds a phase-aware delay before prefill steals decode batches when decode is mid-gen. it's on test branch `phase-steal-slowdown`

alex: perfect — if tests look good, let's run a 1-hour canary sweep overnight. prioritize regions with mixed short/long seq traffic

perf-bot: perf ticket RI-4127 created: "canary p95 regression after batching handoff; suspected kernel fallback + KV priming noise" (link: https://internal.redwood/RI-4127)

maria: thanks — i'll update the rollout doc with the rollback conditions (>=10% p95 regression OR >4% throughput drop)

nina: quick note — include memory HWM and CUDA kernel stall traces in the checklist. those were helpful last time

alex: cool. i'll follow up with the profiler output and a small flamegraph dump later today

maria: sounds good. good catch everyone :thumbsup:
